name: zod
description: TypeScript-first schema validation with static type inference
one_liner: A tool developers use to make sure the data flowing through their app is actually in the shape it's supposed to be.
buyer: No direct buyer — this is foundational developer infrastructure, not something a business pays for on its own.
business_use_cases: A dev team uses it under the hood to validate API requests and form input, invisible to the end business.
A SaaS platform relies on it to reject malformed data before it reaches the database, reducing support tickets from bad input.
An agency building client web apps standardizes on it to catch data-shape bugs before they reach production.

money_ideas.idea: Sell paid training or a course on advanced TypeScript validation patterns built around it.

steal_this: Not a business opportunity by itself — it's plumbing other products are built on top of, not a product a non-technical buyer would ever pay for directly.
